subtitle: Heart-healthy, diabetes-friendly Indian meals for an 80-year-old. Small portions, low salt, no added sugar, and plenty of vegetables, dal, nuts and fruit.
safety: Check with the doctor or a dietitian before changing the diet, especially with diabetes tablets or insulin (to avoid low sugar) or a blood thinner.
Blood thinner (warfarin): keep green leafy vegetables like palak and methi about the same amount every week. Do not suddenly add a lot or stop them.
Plate: half vegetables, a quarter dal, paneer or curd, and a quarter rice or roti. About 1 small cup of cooked rice or 2 small phulkas per meal.
Salt: less than 1 teaspoon a day in total. Skip pickles, papad, chips and salted nuts.
Oil: 3 to 4 teaspoons a day (groundnut, mustard or rice-bran). Ghee only a few drops.
No added sugar, jaggery or honey. Eat whole fruit instead of juice. Avoid grapefruit, which interacts with some heart medicines.
Drink 6 to 8 glasses of water a day, unless the doctor has limited fluids. Eat dinner early, by 7:30 pm.
Low sugar (shaky, sweaty, confused): take half a glass of fruit juice or 3 glucose tablets right away, then call the doctor.
